gen-gf-grandstander-gf-courier-prime: Loud, loose, and cheerful up top. Grandstander does its best work shouting with open, uniform lines, while Courier Prime, a monospace, goes quietly to work with a drafting-pen steadiness.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-days-one: Chunky and playful, with a rope-ladder rhythm underneath. Days One has a tall x-height that fills the line, so give it modest sizing, and let Grandstander's short ascenders carry the noise.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-epunda-sans: Grandstander draws every stroke at a single width, curves included, with short ascenders and a tall x-height. Epunda Sans slips in below with oversized, light-filled counters, and the two share the space without crowding each other.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-farro: Farro keeps its ascenders compressed and its strokes free of any contrast, a friendly plain sans. Grandstander is the one built to show off; Farro is the one built to be read.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-fragment-mono: Precise and structured, Fragment Mono lines its letters up like nails on a ruler beneath Grandstander's bold, expressive heading. Their strongest quality is the gap between swagger and order.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-geist-mono: Short ascenders, a tall x-height, and uniform strokes mark Grandstander. Geist Mono, a monospace with fixed-width code-style letters and generous side gaps, makes the pair feel like play next to precision.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-genos: Grandstander looks bent from a single length of tubing, with open letters and bold expression. And Genos, tightly spaced with a high midline and a mild stroke contrast, keeps the text moving without a snag.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-geom: Fat, friendly, and a bit show-offy. Geom follows with a lofty lowercase band, a sans that gives Grandstander's calligraphy-free outlines something tidy to stand next to.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-hammersmith-one: Grandstander is the showman here, bold and expressive, with open letters and short ascenders. Hammersmith One does the quieter job, its plain sans rounded strokes like cut cord, and capitals barely taller than lowercase.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-inder: Rounded, bold, and a little cheeky. Grandstander and Inder make a strong pair because the heading's curves and straights share one line width, while the sans-serif body stays clean and professional.
